رَاغِمٌ : see 1. You say, هُوَ رَاغِمٌ and رَاغِمُ الأَنْفِ [He has the nose cleaving to the dust: and hence,] (assumed tropical:) he is abased, or humble, or submissive: and (assumed tropical:) he is unable to obtain his right, or due: and [رُغْمٌ is its pl.:] you say, هُمْ رُغْمُ الأُنُوفِ. (Har p. 369.) And دَاغمٌ is used as an imitative sequent thereto. (K.) ―
-b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Angry. (TA.) ―
-b3- And (assumed tropical:) Disliking, disapproving, or hating. (TA.) ―
-b4- And (assumed tropical:) Fleeing. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
